message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** VM on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Create a project‑specific zone (e.g., us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Pick a machine type that supports GPUs – e.g., n1-standard‑8
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 3. Name your instance
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# 4. Create the instance with:
#    • 1 RTX A6000 GPU
#    • Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal)
#    • Preemptible (optional) – remove --preemptible if you want a regular instance
#    • 100 GB persistent disk (adjust size as needed)
#    • Default network & subnet
#    • Allow SSH via metadata key
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=focal-v20231101 \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --preemptible   # <-- remove this flag if you don't want a preemptible instance
```

> **Notes**
> * `--image-family=focal-v20231101` points to the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image at the time of writing. You can replace the version tag with the one you prefer.
> * The `startup.sh` script (if you have one) can install CUDA, cuDNN, or any other software you need right after boot.
> * The `--tags` option opens ports 80/443 so you can expose a web service later.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (or embed it into a Terraform / Pulumi module), here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}
Content-Type: application/json
```

### Request Body

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-demo",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced",
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/focal"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/us-central1-a/types/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-11-8"
      }
    ]
  },
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false
  }
}
```

> Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual values.  
> The `sourceImage` field uses the family `focal`, which always resolves to the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.  
> The `guestAccelerators` block attaches one RTX A6000 GPU.  

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Machine type (`n1-standard-8`) – supports GPUs |
| ✅ | Accelerator (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`) – 1 GPU |
| ✅ | Image family (`focal`) – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| ✅ | Disk size/type – 100 GB balanced SSD |
| ✅ | Network – default VPC + external NAT |
| ✅ | Metadata – optional startup script |
| ✅ | Scopes – full cloud‑platform access |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or add more GPUs if your workload demands it. Happy computing!
